surfaces.part: header cap (red band with a white highlight)

answer.evidence: The sign is a tall, flat, face-on board. The header (rows 0-4) is a front-facing strip with chamfered corners (width 9, then 11, then 13). The same crimson fill continues down the column at x=7, and a dark line at row 5 follows it. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse, so I read it as a 1-2 row cap or rim rather than a top surface. The board (rows 6-28) is a vertical face with lettering, and the grey base (rows 29-31) is a front strip. No horizontal surface is visible anywhere, so it reads as a front elevation, not three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin vertical sign panel with a dark red body, a lighter border and light glyphs. It reads as about 4 lightness steps on the red ramp (dark edge, body, inner highlight, border), a little fewer than the references. Measured facts: 7 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) but below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, better than bus-shelter-a (9%), so the glyphs and border break up the panel. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans dark red rather than black, which fits the dark-material-tone treatment. By eye it is a little flatter and plainer than the kiosk and vending machine, but a sign panel is a simple object. It sits at the level of the bus shelter, which is accepted shipped art, so an artist would accept it beside the references.

surfaces.part: main sign board with cream lettering

answer.evidence: The sign is a flat upright board. Rows 6-29 are a dark red panel with cream lettering, drawn face-on, with a grey base at row 30. The top header (rows 0-4) is a slightly lighter red (L=59) than the panel (L=38), with a white glint at row 1 and rounded corners (widths 9, 11, 11, then 13). It ends in a darker row 4 and a dark outline row 5. That reads as a front-facing header strip or rounded hat, not a horizontal surface seen from above. It has no ellipse width profile, no clear front-edge line with eave shadow, and no contents. At most 1-2 rows could be a rim. The width stays at 13 for rows 3-31, so no side face is drawn. This is borderline, but the top is not convincing as a top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small vertical sign about 12x22 source pixels. The dark edge pixels are 0% near-neutral, so the outline leans red-brown rather than black, matching the tinted outlines of the references. It has 7 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, versus 9% for bus-shelter-a, so there are no large flat fills; the glyphs and rim break up the face. It is a thin single-tile prop, so by eye it looks a little simpler than kiosk-a and vending-a. It is still at least as rich as bus-shelter-a, which is accepted shipped art, and it does not read as a flat black-outlined sticker.
